ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners with a direct or indirect interest of 25% or more, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list, the Special Economic Measures Act regulations, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HMT and EU sanctions lists, Canada's Criminal Code terrorist entity listing, and Ontario enforcement notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any domestic or foreign politically exposed person, including family members and close associates, using independent source-of-funds verification and documented risk scoring. Client identification, verification, and ongoing monitoring records must be retained for at least seven years in accordance with FINTRAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ServiceOntario - Ontario Business Information System (ONBIS), available through www.serviceontario.ca; NUANS name search through www.nuans.com
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed limited partnership name must be in Latin script. Non-Latin names must be transliterated into a Romanized form. The name must include a legal element such as 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', 'L.P.' or 'société en commandite' / 'SEC'. The name must be distinctive, distinguishible from existing registered names in Ontario, and must not be misleading or contravene the Ontario Business Names Act or the Limited Partnerships Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, ServiceOntario will issue a notice stating the grounds. Within 30 days of that notice, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director, Companies and Corporations Branch, ServiceOntario, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, setting out grounds of distinctiveness, legal suitability, and non-violation of naming rules. Any required ministerial consents or authorization letters for sensitive tokens must accompany the request. If the Director declines to overturn the rejection, the applicant may commence judicial review before the Divisional Court of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, within the applicable statutory limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered agent's office is accepted by ServiceOntario for limited partnership registration only if it is a physical street address in Ontario at which service of process can be validly effected; a post-office box is not acceptable. For the offshore supply vessel leasing industry, a virtual office alone is commercially inadequate because Transport Canada, the Canadian Coast Guard, maritime insurers, and enhanced AML/CFT due diligence expect a real operational footprint. A virtual registered office may be used during formation, but a physical Ontario operations office will be expected before active chartering and vessel operation commences.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Transport Canada, municipal business-licensing investigators, or FINTRAC compliance officers within the first 36 months of active operation. The probability exceeds 60% where the limited partnership itself operates and crews vessels under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 rather than limiting its activity to bareboat leasing to a third-party operator.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, as amended, ss. 2, 3, 5, 9 and 12; Limited Partnership Regulations, R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 716
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: ServiceOntario, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Ontario limited partnership. Initial capital contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement; no escrow account is mandated by the Ministry for non-resident limited partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial registered capital and limited partner subscriptions are hereby deemed approved and the General Partner is authorized to issue partnership units against contributions as set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be located at [address in Ontario], and the General Partner engaged to administer the affairs of the Limited Partnership. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed officers for the purpose of statutory filings, banking, and offshore leasing operations: The partnership shall effect all registrations under Canadian law and the Limited Partnerships Act (Ontario). The General Partner is authorized to negotiate, execute, and deliver all documents incidental to the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario – Business Name Search Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS-based name search for the proposed limited partnership name. Ensure the name is not confusingly similar to an existing vehicle chartering or vessel-management entity. Reserve the approved name for 90 days and retain the search report for the filing.
required_dossiers: Identity details of the proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or challenged, file a fresh NUANS search with a revised distinctive element within the same service day; no additional reservation fee is imposed until the second search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and notary public authorized by the Province of Ontario
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the limited partnership agreement in writing and execute Form 1 Declaration. The general partner must verify true identities and the extent of limited to non-managerial investors. Notarize the general partner's signature if required by the financial institution or foreign bank involved in the offshore lease escrow.
required_dossiers: Identification and address of general and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure incomplete schedules by executing a supplementary declaration or amendment and resubmitting the corrected Form through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form 1 via the online business registration portal or prescribed service window. Pay the statutory registration fee. Obtain the Ministry's acceptance receipt. No certificate is a substitute for the tax registrations that follow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing statutory provisions, amend the declaration and refile within the response period; appeal to the Ministry's adjudicative services if the query exceeds 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt General Partner Board Resolutions and Open Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first meeting of the general partner's board and adopt the pro-forma resolution covering subscriptions, registered office and officers. Immediately notify the registered office of appointment and maintain the minute book in Ontario.
required_dossiers: Certificate or receipt of limited partnership filing
Registered office consent and appointment record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a director objects or a quorum fails, reconvene with the alternate general partner representative and obtain unanimous written consent for the resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Partnership Registration and Tax Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – CRA Business Registration and RC220 Partnership Information Return portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form RC220 and obtain a partnership Business Number. Register the general partner and each limited partner, if applicable, for income tax, GST/HST, and payroll accounts only where relevant to offshore marine chartering activities.
required_dossiers: List of partners and Canadian addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA holds the registration for confirmation, resubmit corrected schedules and provide the partnership number issued by ServiceOntario to demonstrate validity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada – Marine Safety and Security; Canadian Coast Guard for marine safety and emergency response compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Registry and Commercial Marine Operating Clearance under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and Vessel Registration and Tonnage Regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada; Fisheries and Oceans Canada where marine impact is engaged
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Oil discharge limit of 15 ppm, MARPOL Annex V waste retention rules, sulphur cap of 0.10% m/m in North American Emission Control Areas, ballast water management records, and spill response under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection under Part VI of the Ontario Fire Code for shore-base control rooms; Transport Canada marine occupational health and safety clearance and emergency response plan for the chartered offshore supply vessel; structural and load registry documentation for crane and handling systems attached to the vessel; Canadian Coast Guard pollution and incident plan approval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Federal tax administration, including GST/HST, customs duties, and business number registration; Ontario Ministry of Finance — Provincial tax and benefit administration, with the HST provincial component collected by CRA under the HST harmonization arrangement. Principal registration portal: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) / My Business Account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must obtain a Canadian Business Number (BN) through the CRA's Business Registration Online portal or by filing Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number'. The partnership registers for a GST/HST program account if it makes taxable supplies in Canada (other than zero-rated supplies) in excess of the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, or voluntarily to claim input tax credits and to charge GST/HST on taxable supplies. The BN is the statutory corporate and partnership tax identifier; Ontario does not issue a separate provincial TIN for HST purposes, as the HST is collected by the CRA on behalf of the Province of Ontario. For excise and customs matters, the partnership may also require a Canadian Customs Business Number and a registered importer/exporter account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A limited partnership is tax-transparent under the Canadian Income Tax Act and the Ontario Taxation Act; income, gains, and losses flow through to partners in proportion to their partnership interests. For GST/HST purposes, the partnership is a separate person from its partners. Non-resident partners are subject to Canadian tax only if the partnership carries on business in Canada and the partner is a member of the partnership. The partnership is not subject to entity-level federal or Ontario corporate income tax unless a specific election applies to treat it as a corporation for foreign tax purposes under domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime. A Canadian limited partnership is pass-through by default; no election exists to convert it to a taxable entity for domestic purposes. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) an election under subsection 97(2) of the Income Tax Act to defer recognition of gain or loss on property contributed to the partnership; (ii) a partnership election under section 10 of the Income Tax Act with respect to inventory of a business; (iii) for GST/HST purposes, a partnership and a partner may jointly elect under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act to deem certain supplies by the partner to be made by the partnership; and (iv) foreign tax and hybrid mismatch elections may be required under the OECD/G20 BEPS Action 2 framework, as reflected in the Canadian hybrid mismatch rules in sections 94.8 to 94.26 of the Income Tax Act. No domestic election permits a limited partnership to be taxed as a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); in Ontario the applied rate is HST combining 5% federal GST and 8% provincial PST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small-supplier threshold under section 148(1) of the Excise Tax Act), computed on taxable supplies made in Canada, other than zero-rated supplies, in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. A non-resident engaged in commercial activity in Canada must register when the threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is permitted to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not require real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices for GST/HST purposes. Electronic invoices and supporting records are accepted provided they are intelligible, reliable, and retain data integrity. Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns applies to registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million, and all registrants may file electronically through the CRA's My Business Account. Ontario does not impose separate e-invoicing clearance obligations beyond the federal electronic filing regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, a supply of goods (including a marine vessel) that is exported from Canada by the supplier, or supplied to a non-resident for removal from Canada, may be zero-rated if the supplier retains satisfactory documentary evidence of the export and the goods are actually exported within a reasonable time. For an offshore supply vessel leased by a Canadian limited partnership to a non-resident owner/operator, the lease supply may qualify for zero-rating as (i) a supply of goods for export, (ii) a supply of a vessel for use outside Canada, or (iii) a supply of a transportation service if the vessel is used predominantly in international transportation. If the vessel is leased for use within Canadian territorial waters, continental shelf operations, or in the exploration/exploitation of Canadian natural resources, the supply will generally be subject to HST at 13%. The supplier must obtain a documented declaration from the non-resident recipient confirming that the vessel is being exported or used exclusively outside Canada, and must retain export documentation and evidence of consideration conclusively linking the supply to export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Customs Coding Form B13A or EDI approved exporter report)
Bill of Lading / Waybill showing exporter, foreign consignee, vessel identification, loading port, and foreign discharge port
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank documentation confirming receipt of foreign currency consideration within the prescribed repatriation period
Booking confirmation or charter party agreement in case of vessel leasing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the CRA determines that a zero-rated export claim is unsupported or that the vessel was not genuinely exported, the supply is reassessed as taxable at 13% HST, and the partnership is liable for the tax plus statutory interest from the original filing date. A false statement or omission on a GST/HST return that reduces the net tax may attract a civil penalty under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the amount sought to be evaded. In cases of wilful evasion or fraudulent export zero-rating, criminal prosecution may result in fines of up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment for up to five years. The CRA may also audit the partnership's export documentation and, under the joint and several liability provisions applicable to partnerships, any partner may be assessed for the partnership's tax, penalties, and interest. Retrospective clawbacks can extend for a statutory limitation period generally four years after the filing date, or ten years in the case of misrepresentation attributable to neglect or carelessness.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority; Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control bureau. FX administration is coordinated among the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential FX risk, FINTRAC for AML and cross-border transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, Global Affairs Canada for economic sanctions, and the Department of Finance Canada for Currency Act administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, so no exchange-control approval or profit-remittance licence exists for any current or capital transaction. This Ontario Limited Partnership (CA_LP) may receive equity contributions from non-resident partners and remit charter-hire profits or partnership distributions in CAD or USD without Bank of Canada or OSFI clearance; the only legal gates are Part XIII Income Tax Act withholding on non-resident distributions (treaty-reduced where applicable), FINTRAC reporting obligations, and Canadian/OFCAC sanctions screening. CAD/USD conversion executes at interbank spreads with no surrender ratio or conversion quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable: Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation window for export or charter proceeds. Offshore supply-vessel charter revenues may be retained indefinitely in USD in a Canadian bank account. The sole compliance requirement is FINTRAC reporting of international electronic funds transfers and cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more, with the Canadian financial institution filing the report automatically; the bank will require a stated commercial purpose in every wire instruction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Maritime Charter Escrow Account / Operational Account (CAD and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / USD Clearing Concentrator
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with Auto-Sweep to Escrow
Trade Finance Operational Account / Commercial Letter of Credit Facility
USD Settlement Account / Escrow Maritime Rail
Niche Asset-Finance Account / Quebec Marine Corridor

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Offshore digital EMI providers are not authorised deposit-taking institutions in Canada and cannot hold regulated maritime escrow, issue standby or commercial letters of credit, or provide fiduciary clearing services. A foreign EMI must register with FINTRAC as a money-services business and, if engaged in retail payments, with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act; it may serve only as an ancillary low-value collection or disbursement rail and may never replace a Schedule I bank account for statutory escrow or primary treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid with a strong in-person presumption for offshore-managed limited partnerships. If the Ontario LP's general partner is a Canadian-resident corporation, remote video onboarding with e-signature is accepted by all Tier-1 banks. If the general partner or any ultimate beneficial owner is non-resident, the bank mandates at least one physical or supervised-video interview at the Toronto commercial-banking centre for the GP signatories; apostilled or consular-legalised identification may substitute for in-branch document verification, but the bank will additionally require the Ontario extra-provincial LP registration certificate and a complete Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner and multi-tiered UBO chain involving trusts, foundations, or offshore holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Limited Partnerships Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16) registration certificate, notarised ISC/UBO register, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for every direct or indirect interest of 25% or more, and a Canadian legal opinion attesting to the LP's existence and the GP's authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and OFAC exposure from high-risk maritime jurisdictions (flag state, crew nationality, ports of call, charterer or bareboat counterparty)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sanctions-clearance matrix covering Global Affairs Canada, OFAC, and UNSC lists for all vessel IMO numbers and flag registries, AIS voyage logs, charter-party schedule with all beneficial owners of the fleet, and negative media plus PEP screening reports for each counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency USD flows and intercompany transactions to bank-secrecy treasury hubs inconsistent with the stated charter cycle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 60/90-day treasury and FX cash-flow forecast, GP board minutes approving the payment-routing policy, transfer-pricing documentation, and 24-month audited financial statements of the fleet chartering entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to evidence the statutory vessel licence or class certification of the platform supply ships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Registry issued under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, or accepted flag-state equivalent, IMO/class society certificates (ABS, DNV, or ClassNK), P&I cover note, and the ISIC 5222 offshore marine charter commercial model statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow-maritime rail triggering enhanced engagement or money-services expectations at the clearing bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow and trust deed naming the Canadian bank as escrow agent, complete beneficial-ownership and instruction-rights register of the escrow account, and three years of client-identification and transaction records available for FINTRAC audit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident GP/LP capital contributions must arrive via SWIFT MT103 to the CA_LP's account at a Schedule I bank, with field 70 reading 'Capital Injection - Ontario Limited Partnership' and a pre-cleared source-of-funds attestation held on file. CAD funds settle over Payments Canada LVTS with immediate finality; USD funds clear through the bank's US correspondent via Fedwire or CHIPS. FINTRAC's international EFT report is triggered automatically for amounts of CAD 10,000 or above. Charter-hire collections from offshore operators should be lock-boxed to the Maritime Charter Escrow Account at a zero balance, then contractually swept to the operating account upon the weekly charter-payment certificate; release instructions require the GP's countersignature and the escrow agent's reconciliation of the hire invoice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine operational disbursements (bunkers, crew payroll, insurance, port dues, dry-dock maintenance) flow by SWIFT MT103 to overseas beneficiaries and via Payments Canada LVTS or ACSS to Canadian payees, each supported by an invoice package and the bank's sanctioned purpose code. Vessel spares and equipment acquisitions above CAD 250,000 use a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT707) issued by the Canadian bank under UCP600, with the fleet class certificate as the compliance document. Contractor and charterer performance obligations may be back-stopped by standby letters of credit (MT760). The Escrow Maritime rail requires the bank to act as independent trustee, releasing funds only against a charter-party payment certificate, demurrage calculation sheet, and dual-signature instruction from the GP and the vessel operator.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts in 10-day and 1-to-24-month tenors under an ISDA 2002 master or Canadian Master Forwards Agreement; since CAD is fully convertible, these trade on the CLS-settled deliverable market curve rather than at a non-deliverable discount.
Plain-vanilla CAD/USD FX swaps for near-dated liquidity bridging and escrow-sweep funding.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps pairing USD charter-revenue streams against CAD debt service for matched cashflow liability management.

Vanilla over-the-counter currency options, including participating forwards and zero-cost collars, to hedge projected USD charter-hire receipts, subject to derivatives onboarding and an ISDA Credit Support Annex.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in Canada but are not market-prevalent for CAD because the deliverable CLS market functions freely; a CAD NDF may be contracted only with a non-resident counterparty at bank discretion if treasury policy requires alignment with a non-deliverable currency basket.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Return (LP Form 4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the first anniversary and each subsequent anniversary of the LP's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: Registrar issues notice; if not remedied within 60 days, LP registration is administratively cancelled, general partners lose limited liability shield.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency Partnership Information Return (Form T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period (e.g., 31 May for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.229: CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; criminal sanctions for deliberate omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Register of Limited Partners Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the Limited Partnership (maintained by General Partner; no external government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the LP's registration anniversary; must be completed alongside the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee; failure to maintain the register is an offence under the Limited Partnerships Act (Ontario), featuring fines up to CAD 5,000 and potential loss of limited liability protection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No entity-level statutory audit requirement under the Limited Partnerships Act (Ontario). Mandatory independent audit may be triggered by (a) lending institution covenants requiring audited financial statements, (b) the LP agreement expressly requiring an audit, (c) status as a reporting issuer under the Securities Act (Ontario), or (d) terms of a federal maritime charter licence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For a private Ontario-limited partnership, financial statements are prepared under Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS if the partnership is publicly accountable or the general partner is a reporting issuer; partnership income is computed under GAAP as adjusted by the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, on the LP's registration anniversary, the general partner must confirm the accuracy of the register of limited partners, noting any transfers or contributions of partnership interests. The register must record each limited partner's name, address, contribution, dates of contributions, and transfers. Confirmation is internal; no public UBO filing is required at the provincial level for an Ontario LP unless the general partner is a corporation subject to Ontario's significant control registry rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (of the General Partner, if corporate)
